podcast.body: Radiohead recorded this song as a potential theme for the James Bond film "Spectre," but it was ultimately rejected by the movie's producers for being "too dark." The official theme was given to Sam Smith's "Writing's on the Wall." Radiohead later released their version digitally and as the B-side to the "Burn the Witch" 7-inch single. "Alright, well, let's have a listen to what Radiohead did. There's there, failed James Bond movie. And it's also called Specter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Radiohead wrote and recorded a song specifically titled "Spectre" during the sessions for their album "A Moon Shaped Pool," intending it as their second submission for the 2015 James Bond film. Despite their efforts, the song was rejected by the producer, who deemed it "too melancholy" to open the film. It was later released as a free download on SoundCloud and appeared as B-sides and bonus tracks. "They threw everything they had into this song. But in the end, it was also rejected because the producer thought it was two-mellon collie to open the film."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
